newsitem.title: USA: CME lumber ends limit up on strong cash, rumors.
newsitem.headline: CME lumber ends limit up on strong cash, rumors.

text.p: November and January CME lumber futures closed up the daily limit of $10.00 per tbf as a strong cash market and rumors on the Canadian quotas pushed futures up into buy stops and new contract highs.
November closed limit up at $375.70 per tbf and January limit up at 4384.50. Other months finished $8.10 to $3.10 higher with only November not posting a new contract high.
Random Lengths quoted cash spruce at $378 per tbf, up $12 from last week. This, coupled with supply concerns due to a quota on Canadian lumber, sparked the rally in futures, traders said.

They noted rumors that some mills in both Alberta and Quebec may have already exported their yearly allotment under the quota. Canada delayed its announcement on individual quota allocations under the U.S./Canada lumber trade agreement which caused confusion over future exports and sparked the rumors, sources said.
"Regardless if there is any fact to them (rumors), it just makes people nervous to be short," said Neil Schmaedick, Smith Barney Forest Products analyst.
